name: Real Madrid
description: The Santiago Bernabéu is an 81,044-seat footballing temple in the heart of Madrid that has hosted five UEFA Champions League finals and stands as the definitive symbol of Real Madrid's century of dominance. Completely redeveloped between 2019 and 2023, the stadium features a retractable roof and a striking 360-degree illuminated titanium facade, making it one of the most spectacular sporting venues on the planet.

name: Atlético de Madrid
description: The Cívitas Metropolitano is a sweeping 68,456-seat elliptical arena in the east of Madrid that opened in 2017 and hosted the UEFA Champions League final just two years later. Its continuous roof, steep stands, and the ferocious noise generated by the colchonero faithful combine to make it one of the most intimidating home fortresses in European football.

name: Real Sociedad
description: The Reale Arena is a 39,500-seat stadium in the heart of San Sebastián that was extensively rebuilt between 2016 and 2019 to bring the stands dramatically closer to the pitch and transform the match-day atmosphere. Set against the green Basque hills with the river Urumea nearby, it offers a modern yet fiercely authentic experience that reflects the independent spirit of Basque football culture.

name: Real Betis
description: The Estadio Benito Villamarín is a 60,720-seat icon in the Heliópolis district of Seville that has stood as Real Betis's proud home since 1929, repeatedly modernised while retaining its grand old-school grandeur. The fierce devotion of the Béticos creates one of Spanish football's most passionate atmospheres, which reaches its ferocious peak during the intense cross-city derby against rivals Sevilla.

name: Sevilla FC
description: The Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán is a 43,883-seat fortress in central Seville, opened in 1958 and long regarded as one of the most intimidating grounds in Spanish football thanks to its steep, close-set stands and the relentless noise of the sevillista faithful. As the home of the most decorated club in UEFA Europa League history, it has witnessed countless legendary European nights that have cemented Seville's status as a major continental football city.

name: Villarreal CF
description: The Estadio de la Cerámica is a compact 23,500-seat arena in the small city of Villarreal that belies its modest size with a remarkable European pedigree earned through consistent appearances in UEFA competition. Named after the ceramics industry that defines the region, the stadium's famous Yellow Submarine atmosphere and the tight proximity of its passionate fans to the pitch make it one of La Liga's most characterful grounds.

name: Girona FC
description: Estadi Montilivi is a compact 13,450-seat ground in the historic Catalan city of Girona that has been the club's home since 1970 and became an unlikely stage for UEFA Champions League football when Girona made their historic European debut in 2024. The stadium's intimate dimensions and the feverish noise of the local support make every home fixture an electric occasion, ensuring visiting sides rarely find it a comfortable place to play.

name: CA Osasuna
description: El Sadar is a tightly packed 23,576-seat stadium in the ancient Navarrese capital of Pamplona where the club's famously loyal fanbase have supported Osasuna through triumph and adversity since the original ground opened in 1967. The modern covered bowl, completed in its current form in 2020, traps noise to create an intensity of atmosphere that makes Osasuna one of the toughest home environments to visit anywhere in La Liga.

name: RC Celta de Vigo
description: Estadio Abanca-Balaídos is a 29,000-seat historic ground on Spain's Atlantic coast in the Galician city of Vigo, first opened in 1928 and substantially expanded with new stands built for the 1982 FIFA World Cup. The notoriously wet Galician climate, the passionate and vocal Celta supporters, and the stadium's distinctive multi-era architecture combine to create one of La Liga's most atmospheric and memorable match-day experiences.

name: RCD Mallorca
description: The Visit Mallorca Estadi, popularly known as Son Moix, is a 23,142-seat stadium on the Mediterranean island of Mallorca that has served as the club's home since 1999 and was substantially upgraded in subsequent years. Its open south end offers a unique backdrop of island sunshine and pine-clad hillsides, making it one of the most visually distinctive venues in La Liga and a compelling destination for football tourists.

name: Rayo Vallecano
description: The Estadio de Vallecas is a uniquely intimate 14,708-seat ground embedded in the tight streets of the Vallecas neighbourhood in south-east Madrid, where supporters stand barely metres from the pitch and the atmosphere is impossibly intense for a stadium of its scale. Rayo Vallecano's enduring reputation as a club of the people is embodied in every corner of this raw, unpretentious arena, which is beloved by football romantics across Spain and beyond.

name: Getafe CF
description: The Coliseum Alfonso Pérez is a 17,393-seat ground in the industrial city of Getafe, south of Madrid, that has been the club's home since 1998 and is renowned for generating an atmosphere that far exceeds what its modest size might suggest. With the stadium embedded in a working-class community that views the club with fierce local pride, it becomes particularly electric during south-Madrid derbies against Leganés and Rayo Vallecano.

name: RCD Espanyol
description: The RCDE Stadium is a sleek, modern 40,500-seat arena opened in 2009 in Cornellà de Llobregat on the south-western outskirts of Barcelona, giving Espanyol one of the most architecturally striking grounds in Spanish football. Its perfect circular geometry, sweeping continuous roof, and state-of-the-art facilities make it a formidable home fortress for the Pericos, particularly charged during high-stakes matches against city rivals Barcelona.

name: CD Leganés
description: The Estadio Municipal de Butarque is a compact 11,454-seat ground in the southern Madrid suburb of Leganés, redeveloped in 2014 to meet La Liga standards and standing as a testament to a club that has fought its way up from the lower tiers of Spanish football. Small, loud, and fiercely partisan, Butarque is an especially hostile environment for visiting teams during south-Madrid derbies, when the local pride of the pepineros faithful is at its most intense.

name: Real Valladolid
description: Real Valladolid's Estadio José Zorrilla is a compact 27,844-seat ground in the heart of Castile, giving the club a passionate home-town atmosphere that punches above the city's size.

name: Inter Milan
description: The Giuseppe Meazza, universally known as San Siro, is a 75,817-seat monument to Italian football where Inter Milan have won three European Cups and countless Serie A titles in front of one of the world's most passionate fanbases. The stadium's soaring triple-tiered stands, iconic spiral ramps, and the ferocious noise of the Curva Nord make it the beating heart of Inter's identity and one of the most electrifying sporting venues on earth.

name: AC Milan
description: The Giuseppe Meazza, known to the world as San Siro, is a 75,817-seat temple where AC Milan have lifted seven European Cups and cemented their place among the sport's immortal clubs. Shared with city rivals Inter since 1947, its cavernous interior, dramatic tiered architecture, and the red-and-black passion of the Curva Sud create an atmosphere as intense and unforgettable as anywhere in world football.

name: Juventus
description: The Allianz Stadium is a sleek 41,507-seat arena in northern Turin that opened in 2011 as the first Italian ground to be entirely owned and operated by the club it was built for. With stands brought close to the pitch, a continuous enclosing roof, and first-class facilities throughout, it has established itself as one of Serie A's most formidable and modern home fortresses.

name: SSC Napoli
description: The Stadio Diego Armando Maradona is a 54,726-seat colossus in Naples's Fuorigrotta district, renamed in 2020 as a permanent tribute to the Argentine genius who transformed both the club and the city during his legendary years in the 1980s. Built for the 1963 Mediterranean Games and upgraded for the 1990 FIFA World Cup, it remains an intensely emotional venue where Maradona's memory is revered and the passion of the Neapolitan tifosi burns as fiercely as anywhere in Italy.

name: AS Roma
description: The Stadio Olimpico is a 70,634-seat historic arena beside the Tiber where AS Roma have contested decades of Serie A battles and memorable European nights that define the club's identity. Shared with city rivals Lazio, it crackles with singular intensity during the Derby della Capitale, widely regarded as one of the most ferocious and emotionally charged fixtures in all of world football.

name: SS Lazio
description: The Stadio Olimpico is a 70,634-seat grand arena on the banks of the Tiber in Rome, originally completed in 1937 and rebuilt for the 1990 FIFA World Cup, that has hosted Olympic Games, World Cup finals, and some of the most dramatic European club nights of the modern era. Shared with city rivals AS Roma, it generates an extraordinary electric charge on derby day that cements Rome's reputation as one of the continent's great football capitals.

name: Atalanta BC
description: The Gewiss Stadium is a 21,300-seat arena in Bergamo progressively rebuilt from 2019 into a modern, club-owned fortress that reflects Atalanta's remarkable rise to Champions League regulars. Completely upgraded stands brought tight to the pitch on all four sides have turned the Curva Nord into one of the most ferocious and suffocating home environments in Italian club football.

name: ACF Fiorentina
description: The Stadio Artemio Franchi is a 43,147-seat architectural masterpiece in Florence, designed by Pier Luigi Nervi and completed in 1931, that is recognised as one of the most historically and structurally significant football stadiums in the world. Its helical staircases, cantilevered concrete roof, and landmark clock tower have earned it national monument status, making a matchday here a cultural experience as much as a sporting one.

name: Bologna FC
description: The Stadio Renato Dall'Ara is a 38,279-seat historic oval arena in the heart of Bologna, opened in 1927 and one of Italy's most storied grounds, having hosted matches at both the 1934 and 1990 FIFA World Cups. Its traditional architecture, the warmth of the bolognese tifosi, and the stadium's central place in one of Italy's most culturally rich cities combine to make matchday here a genuinely characterful experience.

name: Torino FC
description: The Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino is a 28,177-seat arena rebuilt for the 1990 FIFA World Cup and named in solemn honour of the legendary Grande Torino team lost in the 1949 Superga air disaster. The weight of that tragedy and the annual Superga pilgrimage made by supporters give this stadium an emotional depth that makes it one of the most profoundly moving grounds in Italian football.

name: Genoa CFC
description: The Stadio Luigi Ferraris, affectionately known as il Marassi after the Genova neighbourhood it calls home, is a 36,685-seat fortress completed in 1911 that is the oldest football ground still in use in Italy. Shared with local rivals Sampdoria, its compact steep terracing and the fierce pride of the tifosi of Italy's oldest football club generate an intimidating, raw atmosphere that few modern stadiums can come close to replicating.

name: Cagliari Calcio
description: The Unipol Domus is a modern 16,416-seat arena opened in 2017 on the waterfront of Cagliari, giving Sardinia's only top-flight club a purpose-built home for the first time in the island's football history. With sea views from the upper tiers, compact stands that keep supporters close to the action, and the fierce island identity of the Sardinian faithful, it delivers a matchday experience unlike any other in Serie A.

name: Udinese Calcio
description: The Bluenergy Stadium, long known as the Dacia Arena, is a modern 25,144-seat arena completed in 2016 in Udine that became one of Italy's benchmark examples of a privately built, club-owned ground. Featuring a fully retractable pitch, four covered stands, and excellent sight lines throughout, it provides one of Serie A's most technically impressive and comfortable matchday environments.

name: Empoli FC
description: The Stadio Carlo Castellani is a compact 16,835-seat ground in the Tuscan town of Empoli that has hosted Serie A football since the 1980s and serves as the proud, unpretentious home of one of Italian football's most resilient smaller clubs. Its modest size belies the atmosphere it produces when fully charged, and it has been central to Empoli's repeated ability to compete in the top division against far wealthier opponents.

name: Parma Calcio
description: The Stadio Ennio Tardini is a 27,906-seat historic ground in the gastronomic capital of Parma, opened in 1923 and named after the long-serving president who oversaw the club's golden era of UEFA Cup, Cup Winners' Cup, and Coppa Italia triumphs in the 1990s. The passionate support of a community that rallied to resurrect their club from financial ruin lends matchdays at Tardini an emotional intensity that makes the ground far greater than the sum of its parts.

name: Hellas Verona FC
description: The Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi is a 39,211-seat concrete bowl in the UNESCO World Heritage city of Verona, built for the 1968 European Athletics Championships and substantially upgraded for the 1990 FIFA World Cup. Its passionate Curva Sud, the romantic backdrop of one of Italy's most beautiful cities, and the ferocious local pride of the gialloblu support combine to make Bentegodi a venue where football's raw tribalism meets Italy's extraordinary cultural richness.

name: Como 1907
description: The Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is a 13,602-seat arena situated directly on the shore of Lake Como, making it arguably the most breathtakingly beautiful setting for professional football anywhere in the world, with the surrounding Alps and the shimmering lake forming a permanent backdrop to play. Como 1907's return to Serie A has transformed this charming century-old venue into one of Italian football's most extraordinary and sought-after matchday destinations.

stadium: Parque de Jogos Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas

stadium: Estádio do Clube Desportivo das Aves
